newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia and India settle wheat dispute.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia and India settle wheat dispute.

text.p: Australia has commercially resolved a long-running dispute with India over the export of one million tonnes of wheat worth about A$200 million.
Nigel Officer, general manager international for the Australian Wheat Board (AWB), told Reuters the dispute had been resolved in recent days.
First shipment for the one million tonnes was expected to be arranged very soon, he said.
"The matter has been resolved in a commercial manner, we are very, very pleased," Officer said.
He declined to indicate whether Australia had been required to cut prices to obtain the resolution.
The agreement opens the way for Australia to export 250,000 tonnes of old crop wheat to India in August-September.
It will then export 750,000 tonnes of new crop wheat in November-December.
This would complete delivery of 2.3 million tonnes of Australian wheat which India contracted to buy in 1997.
Australia had delivered 1.3 million tonnes when India complained about the presence of seed weeds in consignments.
Analysts at the time noted that India's complaints also followed soon after a decline in world market prices of wheat.
India's appetite for imported wheat is expected to remain strong.
AWB estimates have India's 1997/98 (June 30) wheat imports rising by 1.4 million to a total of three million tonnes.
